## Triage: first grade, `enhancement` · `security` · `priority:p2` · `domain:services` · `area:workflow`, `pm:blocked` on #22825. Position: **refuse at the trigger-api door**; core's verifier keeps both forms

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-11T11:55Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. ⛔ Classes, positions and functions only.

- **The position question, answered: the door, not core's export.**
  - `verifyHttpSignature` (`packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts`) is, by its own docblock, "the receiver's half of both forms". It is the one scheme definition for every ObjectStack sender, and our outbound senders still sign body-only (`signHttpBody`), which the ruling keeps as published (§6.2).
  - Dropping the branch in core would leave a published `@objectstack/core` export unable to verify the signatures our own outbound sends. It would also narrow that export's accept set (`Clause-②: yes`) for no inbound gain.
  - The inbound door is where the policy lives. trigger-api refuses a verdict whose `scheme === 'body-only'`. This stays in `domain:services`, and core's branch is not dead: it is the receiver half of the outbound form.
- **Order:**
  - `Blocked-by: #22825` (the guidance) stands, as the ruling sets: no period of time, only that merge.
  - It also builds on PR #22822 (#22806), the uniform refusal: a body-only post becomes one more logged cause behind the same `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`. If #22822 has not landed when #22825 merges, the claimant waits for it. That is ordering in the same function, ⛔ not a new block.
- **The spec docblock** (`ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook`, relay `6108557878` on #6017) rides the same PR under the exception path: describe-only text, with an at-tier contract review. That is the #22806 precedent.
- **Pins:** as filed, plus the four-cause log line. The deprecation warning (`bodyOnlyDeprecationLogged`) goes with the branch at the door.
- `Clause-②: yes`. It narrows the inbound door's accept set, so the changeset states FROM → TO.

## Unlock: `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`

Triage seat (seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-11T15:01Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **The blocker the ruling set is closed:** #22825 (the sender guidance) closed `completed` at 2026-10-11T14:40Z. Ruling B on #22805 waits only for that merge, "not for any period of time".
- **The serial note is met too:** PR #22822 (#22806, the uniform refusal) merged at 2026-10-11T12:04Z. A body-only post therefore becomes one more logged cause behind the same `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`.
- The grade (`6108760218`) stands. The refusal lives at the trigger-api door, and core's `verifyHttpSignature` keeps both forms, because it is the receiver half of our outbound. The `ITriggerApiService` docblock rides the same PR.

Claim: PM loop round 1 · 2026-10-11T18:27Z

Scope: step 3 of ruling B on #22805 (`6108492902`, maintainer 「同意」), positioned by triage (`6108760218`): the trigger-api inbound door refuses a verdict whose `scheme` is `body-only`, with the uniform `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` and nothing enqueued; core's `verifyHttpSignature` keeps both forms. The `ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook` docblock rides the same PR under the exception path (describe-only). Ruling-ref: `6108492902`.
File surface, read on `origin/main` `75b6d6a04`:
- `packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts`: the `handleRequest` verification path refuses `scheme === 'body-only'` as one more logged cause behind the same `401`; `bodyOnlyDeprecationLogged` and its warning (near `:86`, `:234`, `:317`) go with the branch.
- Tests beside the door, in `packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/`, including the `handleInboundHook` member's arm table and the member/mount parity table PR #22873 added.
- `packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts`: description text only; the verification bullet names the timestamped form as the only accepted one. ⛔ No schema shape change. Declared on #6017 in this act (it is also the carrier the at-tier review on PR #22873 asked for).
- Hand-written docs that still tell a sender the inbound door accepts the body-only form: corrected where false, named in the PR.
- `.changeset/22826-*.md` for `@objectstack/trigger-api` (and `@objectstack/spec` for the docblock), FROM → TO.
- ⛔ No change to `packages/core` (`verifyHttpSignature`, `signHttpBody`), to the outbound senders, or to ADR-0138 (its D7 sentence is corrected at that ADR's next revision, ⛔ not here). Stop on breach; explain in the report.
- **Disclosure:** `security`. ⛔ No reproduction recipe on any public surface.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` (`dispatch-gates --tier --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`: "no path-derived mandate"; the default tier). Describe text on a published contract and a breaking narrowing owe a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record before the queue.
Clause-②: no (narrowing)
- It narrows a published door's accept set (the body-only signature form stops verifying), a BREAKING change for a sender still on that form, and widens nothing. Triage's suggestion line read `yes`; it is not taken, because the criterion is widening, and a narrowing is declared `no` with the narrowing arm, which `check-changeset-no-major` reads as breaking.
Responsibility: `n/a — not a defect card`
Thread-read: 6110352531
Serial constraints cleared, at this stamp:
- #22825 (the sender guidance, the ruling's only blocker) closed `completed`; PR #22822 (#22806, the uniform refusal) and PR #22873 (#22774, the `handleInboundHook` member, same file) are both on `main` (`75b6d6a04`).
- No open PR touches `packages/triggers/trigger-api/`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts` or `packages/core/src/security/http-signature.ts` (every open PR's file list read).

## ACCEPT (seat review): PR #22887 at `78b92702d3` · `domain:services` seat 2 (#21118) · `session_013LbZ9MhPp1iriZEtgJqioA` · 2026-10-11T19:37Z

Claim `6112250834`; ruling B on #22805 (`6108492902`), positioned by triage (`6108760218`). Report `6112859544`, checked against GitHub, ⛔ not taken on trust. ⛔ Classes and positions only (`security`).

**Claim amendment (file surface, same round):** the claim's surface grows by four files.
- Two are describe-only edits inside `packages/triggers/trigger-api`: the `plugin.ts` docblock and the `trigger-api-route-ledger.ts` note, both made false by this change.
- Two are test files the whole-repo sweep reached:
  - `packages/qa/dogfood/test/flow-credential-channel.dogfood.test.ts`: its signer drove the real door in the retired form, so the required Dogfood gate would have gone red. The reverse check D showed it.
  - `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.test.ts`: its member double carries the trigger's verifier and now accepts the timestamped form only, a fidelity fix with no new pin.
- Each meets the on-the-spot conditions: same defect class, mechanical, no other claim on the file, same gate family. The PR body names each.

**Checklist, as checked:**
- **PR shape:** draft, base `main`, assignee `zhuangjianguo`. Line 1 `Fixes #22826`, line 2 `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; no other closing keyword.
- **Scope:** 9 files (+226 / −143), 369 changed lines; `check-governed-merges`: 0 of 9 paths governed, under 3,000. Zero `packages/core` lines: `verifyHttpSignature` and `signHttpBody` are untouched. No outbound sender, no ADR-0138 and no `content/docs/releases/` edit.
- **The code, read in full:**
  - One private `verifyInboundSignature` holds the door's judgement: core's verdict, then an exhaustive `switch` on `scheme` that accepts `v1` and refuses `body-only` with the cause `signature-body-only`. `handleRequest` and the exported `verifySignature` both call it, so the export answers as the door does.
  - The refusal sits after the secret read and before the JSON parse and the enqueue. It goes through the existing `refuseUnverified`, the uniform `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE` envelope of #22806.
  - `bodyOnlyDeprecationLogged` and the deprecation line are gone.
  - The `switch` has no default, so a scheme core adds later fails to compile at the door until the door decides it.
- **Pins:** the trigger-api arm, parity and uniform-refusal tables now hold the body-only form to `401` with nothing enqueued, through both the mount and the member. The cause table pins `signature-body-only`. Ablations: A (accept again) 7 red, B (mislabelled cause) 2 red, C (deprecation line back) 1 red, D (old signer against the new door) 7 red. Each was restored by blob.
- **Spec docblock** (`ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook`): describe-only. It names the timestamped form as the only accepted one and the body-only form as refused. The type is unchanged.
- **Hand-written guidance:** the `objectstack-automation` skill's inbound section teaches only the timestamped form, as #22825 left it. The `webhooks.mdx` `sha256=` sentences describe the OUTBOUND contract, which is unchanged. Nothing is owed.
- **Prose surfaces, sentence by sentence against the diff:**
  - The changeset's "What narrows" bullets match the door, the uniform refusal, the cause list and `verifySignature`'s new answer.
  - "Unchanged: the outbound contract" matches the zero `packages/core` diff.
  - "Who sees a difference" names the published guidance, so no recipe is invented.
- **Semver, for the at-tier review to judge:** `@objectstack/trigger-api` is graded `major` (`@objectstack/spec` `patch`). The gate accepts that in `next` pre mode, and the dev cites precedents. `check-changeset-no-major`'s own docblock says a declared narrowing "ships `minor`" during the launch window, and this lane's ADR-0131 narrowings on `main` use `minor`. The seat records the two readings and does not re-grade.
- **CI on `78b92702d3`:** 16 success, 3 skipped, 13 in progress at this stamp, none failed. Landing waits for the run.

**Out of scope, noted:** ADR-0041 (`docs/adr/0041-flow-trigger-family.md`, near `:119`) still names the trigger's HMAC "GitHub/Stripe style". Carrier: that ADR's next revision, beside ADR-0138 D7's correction, which ruling B already assigns. It is governed text, ⛔ not this PR's.

**Landing:** a narrowing and describe text on a published contract owe a `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review of record. `needs:contract-review` goes on the PR in this act, and this seat runs the review with an isolated at-tier reviewer. On PASS with every check green, the PR goes ready and auto-merge. It is not governed and is under the human-merge threshold.
